project_scope.rationale: Pathogen trait (aggressiveness) change linked to a plant pathogen population introduction; plant-pathogen trait relevant to crop disease.

edges.claim_text: The introduction of a new mating type of Phytophthora infestans into European pathogen populations caused an overall increase in aggressiveness of the pathogen.
edges.source_section: Potato late blight, Western Europe, 19th and twentieth
edges.paper: Crop health and its global impacts on the components of food security
edges.quote: As e c o n dm i g r a t i o no fP . infestansprobably occurred in the late 1970s, when a new mating type of the pathogen was introduced in the European populations of the pathogen. This introduction completely changed the genetic structure of European pathogen populations, making the disease more difficult to manage through chemicals (Goodwin et al. 1996) and causing an overall increase in aggressiveness of the pathogen (Day and Shattock 1997).
edges.rejection_reason: Sentence 90 explicitly states the introduction caused an overall increase in aggressiveness of the pathogen; causal wording matches.

project_scope.rationale: Association between a wheat disease and its fungal pathogen is a plant disease/pathogen relationship.

edges.source_section: Fusarium head blight, North America, China, and Europe
edges.paper: Crop health and its global impacts on the components of food security
edges.quote: The disease has been associated with a large number of plant pathogens, but the literature from the USA and Canada mostly refers to Fusarium graminearum (teleomorph Gibberella zeae), while many different Fusarium species are generally considered in Europe (Parry et al. 1995;X u 2003).
edges.rejection_reason: Evidence states the disease is associated with many pathogens and USA/Canada literature mostly refers to Fusarium graminearum; associative modality preserved.

project_scope.rationale: Cropping/tillage practices linked to wheat disease epidemics is an agricultural plant-disease mechanism.

edges.claim_text: Expansion of wheat-maize rotation and conservation tillage practices probably caused particularly severe Fusarium head blight epidemics in North America from the 1990s onward.
edges.source_section: Fusarium head blight, North America, China, and Europe
edges.paper: Crop health and its global impacts on the components of food security
edges.quote: In North America, recurrent epidemics have been reported for many years, but particularly severe epidemics have been taking place from the 1990s until today probably as a result of the expansion of wheat-maize rotation and of conservation tillage practices (Parry et al. 1995;M c M u l l e ne ta l .1997, 2012; Dill- Macky and Jones 2000; Windels 2000;X u 2003;B a t e m a n et al. 2007).
edges.rejection_reason: Evidence says severe epidemics from 1990s probably resulted from expansion of wheat-maize rotation and conservation tillage; 'probably' preserved as causal-with-uncertainty.

edges.paper: Crop health and its global impacts on the components of food security
